subject: Ridgeway go‑live: fast‑lane payments routing prioritization
messages:
From: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.com>
To: Naomi Feldman <naomi.feldman@redwood.com>, Monica Patel <monica.patel@redwood.com>
Cc: Alex Mercer <alex.mercer@ridgewaycap.com>
Date: Tue, 9 Jul 2024 15:02:00 -0700
Subject: Ridgeway go‑live: fast‑lane payments routing prioritization

Hi Naomi / Monica —

Quick ask: Ridgeway (Alex in cc) just confirmed an aggressive production date for their payments product and has a gating requirement they labelled “fast‑lane routing” — essentially a prioritized path for low‑latency, high‑value payment tokens that bypasses certain batching layers for specific tenant keys. They flagged this as critical for their vendor SLAs.

Why this is urgent: Ridgeway is already contracted (deal RDW-2024-042), legal signed, and procurement is blocking the first invoice until this capability is scheduled in an engineering window. If we can’t commit to a timeframe, they’ve signalled they’ll seek an alternate provider for the pilot.

Attachments: I’ve attached the mutual action plan with the milestone they want (see tab “Go‑Live Requirements”).

Ask: can Eng/Product evaluate a scoped implementation or an interim fallback (config flag + routing policy) we can ship in 2–4 weeks? If not, what is the earliest realistic target and what is the minimal acceptance criteria we need for Ridgeway to unblock billing?

Thanks — this is a high‑impact strategic pilot.

—Ben
Senior Enterprise AE | Redwood Inference

From: Markus Klein <markus.klein@redwood.com>
To: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.com>, Naomi Feldman <naomi.feldman@redwood.com>
Cc: Sean Gallagher <sean.gallagher@redwood.com>
Date: Wed, 10 Jul 2024 09:14:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Ridgeway go‑live: fast‑lane payments routing prioritization

Thanks Ben — tagging this to triage. A couple of clarifying Qs before I scope: 

1) Do we have a clear definition for which tokens/requests should take the fast‑lane? (tenant ID only, token value, payment amount threshold?)
2) Expected QPS for the fast‑lane vs background traffic at go‑live (p95 latency target)?
3) Is Ridgeway asking for persistent residency/isolation for these requests or just a routing priority with best‑effort guarantees?

From a product standpoint, options look like:
- Configurable routing policy (shortest path, higher priority queue) — smaller effort, lower isolation guarantees.
- Dedicated warm pool / reserved capacity for their tenant keys — more engineering work and infra cost, but cleaner SLOs.

If Ben/Naomi can forward exact acceptance criteria from Ridgeway, I can do a half‑day spike today and give an estimate (time + risk + rollback path). If this is blocking invoicing immediately, we should consider an interim docs + runbook workaround that Customer Success can operate.

-Markus
Product Manager, Routing & Runtime

From: Naomi Feldman <naomi.feldman@redwood.com>
To: Markus Klein <markus.klein@redwood.com>, Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.com>
Cc: Monica Patel <monica.patel@redwood.com>
Date: Wed, 10 Jul 2024 11:22:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Ridgeway go‑live: fast‑lane payments routing prioritization

Markus — adding details from Ridgeway’s tech ops (copied below). This is verbatim from Alex: 

"We need a routing policy that will (a) tag payment tokens flagged as 'high‑value' (internal threshold $5k), (b) route them to a priority queue that aims for p95 < 80ms, and (c) allow a manual override from Ridgeway ops for replays during the first 2 weeks. Our expected peak QPS for high‑value tokens is ~12 qps, baseline 1–2 qps after hours."

Business impact notes: if we don’t get a firm commit on delivery window, legal will withhold the first invoice (~$120k ARR commitment) until the capability is slated. Ridgeway is a strategic prospect for a vertical play.

Interim workaround suggestion: CS can implement a runbook that applies client‑side throttling + selective retry suppression and supply a signed attestation to Ridgeway so procurement can proceed. That buys us ~3 weeks but is operationally brittle.

Attaching the mutual_action_plan and the doc with Ridgeway's exact acceptance criteria.

—Naomi
Customer Success Manager | Redwood Inference

Regards,

Please let me know if you need me to loop legal/ops directly into product for a scoping call — they’re available tomorrow morning PST.

From: Markus Klein <markus.klein@redwood.com>
To: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.com>, Naomi Feldman <naomi.feldman@redwood.com>, Sean Gallagher <sean.gallagher@redwood.com>
Cc: Monica Patel <monica.patel@redwood.com>
Date: Thu, 11 Jul 2024 11:28:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Ridgeway go‑live: fast‑lane payments routing prioritization

Acknowledged — I ran a quick spike this morning. Summary and commitment options: 

Option A (fast): routing policy + priority queue flag — can be delivered as a config rollout and infra toggle by Aug 2 (internal sprint slot), acceptance criteria: attach header flag, routing precedence, p95 < 100ms under test load (we can run a short perf harness). No dedicated warm pool; best‑effort scheduling.

Option B (SLA): dedicated warm pool and tenant affinity — more work (approx 3 sprints), p95 < 80ms at scale, stronger isolation. Requires infra capacity reservation and budget signoff.

Tradeoffs: Option A meets Ridgeway’s stated capacity (~12 qps) and can be implemented with low product risk. To meet their explicit p95 < 80ms ask we’d need Option B or a short E2E perf tuning window after Option A is live.

My recommendation: commit to Option A with a scheduled perf verification window and a follow‑up plan to move to Option B if perf targets aren’t met. I can schedule the work for the sprint starting Jul 29 and aim for Aug 2 delivery of the toggle and runbook.

Next steps: 
- Ben: confirm Ridgeway will accept Option A + perf verification (they need a signed timeline).
- Naomi / Monica: prepare the runbook and customer‑facing attestation for procurement.
- Sean: I’ll need a capacity guardrail signoff if we must reserve any burst capacity for the verification window.

If everyone is aligned, I’ll produce a short RFC and ETA by EOD.

-Markus
Product Manager, Routing & Runtime
